text: The story keeps wave 2 because EP02 maps to wave 2, although rwb-partner is a wave 4 service in Architecture v5.
why: Template and Rules R5.6 and R5.7 keep the earlier W-MAP wave and raise one conflict gap per service and business epic.
read: Architecture v5 slides 4, 5, 17 and 41; Template and Rules R5.4, R5.6, R5.7.
confirm: Solution architect confirms the wave of the EP02 portal slice at the dependency review.
impact: The story is planned and staffed in wave 2 and builds against wave 0 and wave 1 contracts and fakes; the service runtime baseline follows in wave 4.

text: The partner_user binding is loaded on POST /api/recovery/partner/v1/admin/reference-loads with the table code partner_user, an Idempotency-Key and the approval role from rwb.refload.approver.partner_user.
why: No source publishes a load operation for partner_user; TSD S9 T-A.1 lists six partner operations and none is a reference load, and the legacy reference-load path is rwb-access's API-P4-005 which cannot write rwb_partner under DP-01.
read: TSD S9 T-A.1, T-A.2; legacy RWB-E2-019 sections 3, 12 and 13; DP-01, DP-07.
applied_in: Section 12.1, third row; section 13 build step 1
confirm: Reference data owner and solution architect confirm the path and the table code before the contract freeze.
impact: The load is a stated default on the S9 base and carries no partner portal right; if confirmed otherwise only the path changes and the validation rules of AC2 stand.

text: The partner gateway holds the resolution of RWB-P4-E2019-CON and forwards the partner id, the partner role and the PLACED descriptor on each portal call; this service does not call the resolution operation.
why: The resolution is synchronous one hop from the gateway that fronts the portal, and a second call from the owner would be a second hop inside the same request.
read: Architecture v5 slides 12, 20 and 35; RWB-P4-E2019-CON sections 4 and 12.1; DP-11.
confirm: Gateway owner and the rwb-access owner confirm the descriptor is forwarded on every portal call.
impact: The story consumes the descriptor shape and the refusal vocabulary as its C dependency and holds no session and no token.

text: Each refusal condition maps to the legacy message at its legacy status: MSG-P4-001 at 401, MSG-P4-008 at 401, MSG-P4-002 at 403, MSG-P4-003 at 404, MSG-P7-003 at 503, MSG-GEN-004 at 409 and MSG-GEN-006 at 503.
why: TSD S9 T-A.2 publishes the error codes of the partner operations and no message id per condition.
read: TSD S9 T-A.2; legacy RWB-E2-019 sections 5 and 14; RWB-P4-E2019-CON section 14.
confirm: Business lead and solution architect confirm the mapping at the message review; the texts stay the legacy texts.
impact: The statuses are the legacy ones and the texts are unchanged; a different mapping changes the response status only.

text: partner_user carries DF-REF-212 id, DF-REF-213 identity_ref, DF-REF-214 partner_id, DF-REF-215 role_code, DF-REF-216 valid_from and DF-REF-217 valid_to, with a foreign key to partner.
why: TSD S9 T3.1 has no catalogue entry for partner_user; the Logical Data Model gives the six fields and the legacy story uses the same identities and types.
read: Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8, DF-REF-212 to DF-REF-217; legacy RWB-E2-019 section 11; TSD S9 T3.0.
confirm: Data steward confirms the field list and the foreign key before the DB story freezes the table.
impact: The binding keeps the period fields and no new status column is invented; an ended period is valid_to, not a flag.

text: The firm and binding re-check runs when the cached answer is older than rwb.access.membership-refresh-minutes, assumed at 5 minutes as the legacy story has it.
why: The refresh interval is marked assumed in the legacy story with DL38 and is a parameter, not a Schedule.
read: legacy RWB-E2-019 sections 4 and 13; DL38; DP-06.
confirm: Security administrator confirms the interval with DL38 before the first UAT run.
impact: A firm that leaves the panel loses the portal read within one interval; a shorter interval costs one authorise and one row read per call.

text: A refusal at the owner writes one local decision record with decision code AC-DENY, the reason PARTNER_NOT_ACTIVE or NO_PARTNER_BINDING, actor SY-RWBPART and scopeRef PLACED, keyed by the request; the entry of a resolution stays rwb-access's.
why: DP-03 is in the pattern set and the legacy story records a refusal, while the ledger entry of a sign-in belongs to rwb-access and RWB-P7-E2019-APP.
read: legacy RWB-E2-019 AC3, AC4 and section 17; DP-03; RWB-P7-E2019-APP sections 1 and 4.
confirm: The rwb-decision owner confirms the record code and reason vocabulary at the ledger review.
impact: One decision has one entry: no duplicate ledger entry for a sign-in, and a portal read refused at the owner is still provable.

text: The instruction types of a partner role are read from rwb.access.partner.instruction-types.<ROLE> at its version, with PT-AGENCY=COLLECT assumed as the legacy story has it.
why: The legacy story gives PT-LAWFIRM and PT-VALUER values and marks the PT-AGENCY row assumed with owner RW-AGENCYMG.
read: legacy RWB-E2-019 section 3; DP-06; LOV-INSTRUCTION of TSD S9 T3.2.
confirm: Partner and agency manager confirms the instruction types of each partner role before UAT.
impact: No instruction type is a constant; a role whose parameter is absent reads nothing rather than everything.
